title: Wendell and the Will
premise: When estate lawyer Silas Galloway reads the will of the late Edith Marsh and finds a bequest naming a child who officially never existed, a confession letter postmarked the day after her funeral arrives at his office, implicating three of the town's founding families in a death thirty years past. As Silas investigates, he discovers his own late father helped fabricate the alibis that sent an innocent man to prison, and that Edith spent decades quietly paying restitution. At trial, Silas must choose between protecting the town's living descendants — including the woman he loves — and exposing the truth, ultimately testifying against his own father's legacy and securing the hidden heir her inheritance.
about_author: Petra Voss is a former small-town court clerk who spent a decade transcribing depositions in rural county courthouses before turning to fiction. She writes mysteries about paper trails, buried confessions, and the people who keep secrets professionally.

chapters.title: The Reading
chapters.summary: Silas Galloway reads Edith Marsh's will to a tense gathering of heirs, stumbling over a bequest to 'the girl in the boathouse' — a name no one recognizes. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: unease beneath professional composure.

chapters.title: Postmarked Yesterday
chapters.summary: A day after the funeral, an unsigned confession letter arrives claiming Edith witnessed a killing in 1994. Silas recognizes the handwriting style from old case files. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: dread disguised as curiosity.

chapters.title: Alphabetized Secrets
chapters.summary: Silas searches his firm's archives and finds a gap where the 1994 coroner's file should be — a gap his own father once managed. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: first crack of personal guilt.

chapters.title: The Boathouse Girl
chapters.summary: Silas tracks the will's beneficiary to Lena Voss, now a nurse two counties away, who was smuggled out of town as a child after her mother drowned. POV: Lena. Emotional beat: wary hope meeting suspicion.

chapters.title: Three Families, One Story
chapters.summary: Silas interviews the Aldridge, Crane, and Marsh descendants, whose alibis for the night of the drowning are word-for-word identical. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: the chill of rehearsed truth.

chapters.title: What Edith Kept
chapters.summary: In Edith's locked study, Silas finds thirty years of cash ledgers — payments to the imprisoned man's family, signed simply 'E.M.' POV: Silas. Emotional beat: grief for a stranger's long penance.

chapters.title: Duty Calls
chapters.summary: District Attorney Priya Nair opens an inquiry into the drowning; she and Silas, former lovers, must work together while guarding old wounds. POV: Priya. Emotional beat: love complicated by duty.

chapters.title: The Man in Cell Block C
chapters.summary: Silas visits Tommy Reeve, convicted of manslaughter in 1995, who has stopped proclaiming innocence because hope hurt too much. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: shame hardening into resolve.

chapters.title: Crane's Bargain
chapters.summary: Harlan Crane offers Silas a partnership and hush money, revealing he knows about the letter. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: temptation measured against contempt.

chapters.title: Lena Comes Home
chapters.summary: Lena returns to town incognito and finds her childhood home burned to its foundations years ago — arson never investigated. POV: Lena. Emotional beat: rage kindling into purpose.

chapters.title: Father's Handwriting
chapters.summary: Silas matches the fabricated alibi statements to his father's typewriter ribbon samples and realizes Galloway & Sons built the lie. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: betrayal by the dead.

chapters.title: Witness for the Defense
chapters.summary: The Crane family retains counsel to block the will's probate, forcing Lena's claim into open court and setting a trial date. POV: Priya. Emotional beat: the machinery of law grinding awake.

chapters.title: Night Swimmers
chapters.summary: Lena recalls the last night with her mother: a boat, raised voices on the dock, and Edith Marsh watching from the shore. POV: Lena. Emotional beat: memory as both wound and weapon.

chapters.title: The Second Letter
chapters.summary: A second confession arrives — this one from Harlan Crane's dying sister, admitting she drove the getaway car the night Lena's mother was struck. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: horror at how ordinary the evil was.

chapters.title: Pressure
chapters.summary: Someone ransacks Silas's office; the ledgers vanish. He suspects everyone, including Priya, whose career depends on the old conviction standing. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: isolation sharpening trust issues.

chapters.title: Edith's Tape
chapters.summary: Hidden in the boathouse ruins, Lena finds a cassette: Edith recording what she saw in 1994 and why she stayed silent — they threatened the child. POV: Lena. Emotional beat: sorrow transmuted into testimony.

chapters.title: Pretrial Maneuvers
chapters.summary: Priya moves to vacate Tommy Reeve's conviction while the Cranes move to suppress the tape; Silas is subpoenaed as both lawyer and witness. POV: Priya. Emotional beat: love and duty pulling opposite directions.

chapters.title: The Stand
chapters.summary: Silas testifies about the altered files, damning his father's name publicly; Harlan Crane's counsel disintegrates under cross-examination. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: catharsis through self-destruction.

chapters.title: What Harlan Knew
chapters.summary: Confronted with the tape and ledger copies, Harlan breaks and names his brother as the one who struck Ruth Voss and staged the drowning. POV: Priya. Emotional beat: the collapse of thirty years of silence.

chapters.title: Verdicts
chapters.summary: Tommy Reeve walks free; the elder Crane is indicted; the court validates Edith's will and Lena's inheritance. POV: Lena. Emotional beat: justice arriving too late to feel like victory, but arriving.

chapters.title: Settling the Estate
chapters.summary: Silas executes Edith's final wishes: restoring the boathouse as a memorial, funding Tommy's exoneration, and sealing his father's file with a note of apology. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: grief accepted, not erased.

chapters.title: Open Water
chapters.summary: Months later, Silas and Lena stand at the rebuilt boathouse; Priya visits with news of the trial date, and the three choose to face it together rather than alone. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: cautious love, earned peace.
